answer: One defence is bonded reputation: each agent must lock a stake before joining, and peers slash it when the agent lies or spams. A single whisper of false data then costs real money, so an attacker who spawns thousands of fake agents must fund every one. At dawn of each epoch the network re-scores trust, weighting long-lived honest history over fresh accounts, while a lone fraudster falls into a canyon of lost deposits and honest agents keep earning. Sybil scale becomes an expensive trap instead of a free win.
